text.p: Five men wearing Bill Clinton masks "flashed" for the cameras in front of the U.S. Supreme Court on Monday to mock the president in his legal battle with Paula Jones.
They were joined by a man dancing in a duck costume.

As lawyers for Clinton and Jones, who claims Clinton exposed himself to her in an Arkansas hotel room, argued their cases inside, the men stood on the court steps flipping open their trench coats to show bystanders signs that read "Friend of The Court Briefs." A friend of the court brief is a brief filed in support of a party in a case.
Below-freezing temperatures kept them from showing up as planned in their underwear.
The prancing duck held aloft a sign telling Clinton to "Stop Ducking The Truth."

The demonstration, which included wanted poster-type leaflets with a drawing of Clinton, was organised by the Clinton Investigative Commission, described as a project of the Council of Volunteer Americans, a non-profit watchdog group.
No one was available at the group's suburban Virginia headquarters to comment on questions about the demonstration.
